content: Business invariants and history belong to one named bounded context. Contexts integrate through stable IDs and published contracts; desktop, web, and KiCad-facing shells stay thin composition roots. Avoid ownership-free core, models, or utils modules.

title: Keep SQLite roles physically and logically separate
rationale: The team-authoritative database, each desktop replica, generated KiCad projection, and external read-only databases serve different consistency and authority roles. Synchronize records and regenerate projections atomically; never multi-writer-sync SQLite files.

title: Use PocketBase as the sole team backend
rationale: PocketBase is selected for its maturity, documentation, authentication, realtime, file, migration, hook, job, and backup capabilities. Domain rules remain in application-owned interfaces and protected server-side commands, but the repository will not build an alternate-provider adapter or comparison harness. Pin every PocketBase version and checksum, rehearse upgrades, preserve a canonical export, and prove blank-environment recovery.

title: Use isolated Linux as the primary autonomous integration environment
rationale: AFK runs must be reproducible, parallel-safe, and independent of a developer's Windows KiCad installation and personal state. Required file integration uses an exact pinned official KiCad 10 CLI image; real GUI smoke coverage uses a clean Ubuntu/X11 runner because KiCad does not support its GUI in Docker. Docker Compose provides pinned PocketBase and MinIO services. A scheduled lane tests the newest stable KiCad 10 before advancing the lock, while native Windows and macOS behavior remains a distribution gate.

content: Every frontend seed owns its full autonomous feedback loop: add semantic and accessibility assertions, automate the critical browser or native Tauri journey, capture deterministic screenshots for materially distinct states, inspect actual and diff images, record a concise visual critique, correct every material issue, and rerun. Screenshot review complements behavior tests; baseline changes are explicit and never self-accepted merely because a test changed.

name: Restore PocketBase through an S3-compatible blank-environment drill
description: Use isolated MinIO buckets to test PocketBase backup upload and recovery. Seed records and files, create and checksum the backup, destroy disposable PocketBase state, restore into a blank pinned instance, and compare records, files, hashes, rules, migrations, and version manifest. PocketBase pb_data backups exclude files stored in S3, so any S3-backed application objects require their own replication and restore proof. MinIO proves S3 protocol behavior, not AWS-specific IAM, KMS, TLS, region, or lifecycle configuration.

outcomes.test_results: 16 Rust tests, fmt, clippy -D warnings, manifest check, and source-immutability gate passed; independent review PASS

name: Loss-detecting fixture boundaries fail closed
description: Repository fixture and import oracles classify serialized path syntax lexically rather than with host OS path semantics; accept only exact-case, root-contained regular files; reject traversal and links/reparse points before probing; propagate discovery failures; preserve SQLite NULL distinctly from empty text; and report field-level semantic differences alongside byte identity.

title: Use Docker for application development, not native KiCad execution
rationale: Docker provides the reproducible Rust, frontend, PocketBase, MinIO, and UI-test environment. Linux and Docker do not install or invoke KiCad; the user performs native interoperability checks manually with Windows KiCad, and those checks do not block autonomous product Seeds.
